item.title: Top Version Control Tools: What the Data Shows
item.description: GitLab ranks second in both groups, but the gap is much smaller among those hosting professional projects there. Share of developers, weighted survey results Source: JetBrains Developer Ecosystem Survey 2026. For a public project, GitHub’s familiarity can be an advantage.

item.title: Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes.
item.description: Anyone pointing a new model at a project should ask its maintainers first and come with fixes, not just findings. Reports and fixes stayed on GitHub, where maintainers already work. The result: Codename MDASH, using Microsoft’s MAI Cyber model, flagged thousands of possible issues across the six projects.

item.title: Introducing Azure Catalyst agentic modernization and new AI infrastructure innovations
item.description: This week, we’re introducing innovations across Microsoft Azure that set a new standard for how the cloud powers AI: expanded AI core capabilities in Azure to build what’s next, and Azure Catalyst, an intelligent agent-led solution to modernize the apps, data, and infrastructure that already run the business.

item.title: Genesis AI raises $500 million to deploy glove-wearing robots
item.description: To make his case, Xian hosted TechCrunch at Genesis AI’s Silicon Valley facility, where its physical AI model operated a pair of off-the-shelf robotic arms. The startup’s focus on dexterity — the robot’s ability to do stuff with its hands — and gathering the right data to achieve it sets it apart from competitors like Figure or Agility. For truly generalized robotic intelligence, Genesis needs more data.

item.title: Continuous improvement comes to Microsoft Foundry
item.description: Agents on Foundry get better the more you use them. That means you get the right model for the job, while balancing performance, latency, and cost. Foundry: Running and continuously improving agents at scale Once you’ve built your agent, you need a place to run it, govern it, and improve it for all your teams, in every region, alongside hundreds or thousands of other agents.

item.title: Jordan Belfort’s new AI voice startup, Tone, wants to sell like the ‘Wolf of Wall Street’
item.description: It’s easy to argue the market is already saturated with AI voice startups and technologies, and Tone comes with added risk: Belfort’s co-founder in the business is longtime investor Shervin Pishevar, who has a controversial past of his own. It’s a very unique way of going about building a voice, and it stems from a system of influence and persuasion I’ve been teaching since the late 1980s. One tonality at a time.

item.title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
item.description: Dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks.

item.title: My Cron Job Returns 200 When Every Fetch Fails
item.description: Layer one: an error reporter. Something pings it every 15 minutes, it fetches new jobs per category, scores them against each user's profile with Claude, and emails the good ones. The post calls this a wrong-but-working failure.

item.title: The Simulator, Not the Archive: Your AI SRE Learns Somewhere Else
item.description: Machine learning changes incident remediation only when the agent learns from verified outcomes, not from history. An incident archive records one unrepeatable response per failure, so training on it clones what tired humans did. The simulator, not the archive: the follow-up to the harness argument.

item.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
item.description: Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .

item.title: KubeCon NA 2026 Live: The Identity Crisis of AI Agents and the First Announcements from Salt Lake City
item.description: The identity crisis of agents, the integration of MCP into platforms like OpenShift, and the packaged management of agent skills are not fringe topics but the central construction sites for 2027. The coming months will show whether the outlined solution approaches — per-instance identities, versioned skills, and platform-agnostic AI gateways — prove themselves in practice.

item.title: Security Risks of Deploying Vibe-Coded Apps to Production, and Who Fixes Each One
item.description: The main security concerns with deploying vibe-coded apps to production are code-level flaws the builder never reviewed (injection, broken authorization, insecure defaults), risky dependencies, hardcoded secrets, over-permissive infrastructure, and no record of who changed what.

item.title: GitHub availability report: October 2026
item.description: The short version of October: we added substantial independently scalable Azure capacity and removed several ways that failures could escalate. Actions jobs stayed queued or failed to start because the service that assigns jobs to GitHub-hosted runners stopped working reliably. We traced the failures to the networking issue.

item.title: Two small models ship in my Markdown editor. Three more didn't.
item.description: Each model picks one answer from a fixed list, like which language a code block is in. It got 391 suggestions right at 93.8% precision, against 380 at 93.1% for the model already in the app. Marksage is a Markdown editor I built.

item.title: The Kubernetes Upgrade Trap: A Practical Roadmap to Escape Deprecated APIs, Broken Add-ons, and Endless Delays
item.description: Applications, Helm charts, operators, admission controllers, networking components, storage drivers, monitoring agents, and automation tools must all support the target version. Let's build a practical roadmap that helps teams stop postponing Kubernetes upgrades and start treating them as regular platform maintenance. For example, a workload might still use an API that Kubernetes deprecated several releases ago.

item.title: Rider 2026.3 for Game Development: Lua and Verse Plugins, Better C++ Debugging, and Closer Godot Integration
item.description: This release connects Rider more closely with the Godot Editor, improves debugging for Unreal Engine and custom C++ engines, adds support for Unity CoreCLR Players, and introduces new Lua and Verse plugins in Beta. For a lighter, Verse-focused setup, open the generated .code-workspace file.

item.title: Node.js Document Upload and Signed Download from Private Object Storage for Logistics
item.description: An object key can make operational boundaries obvious: The snapshot ID matters more than the filename. A logistics customer can upload several documents named delivery-note.pdf , and a replacement should not silently change the bytes that an earlier audit refers to. It keeps the authorization decision testable and prevents a storage SDK from becoming the place where tenant policy is hidden.

item.title: Why Genshin Impact Bet on Unity: The Boring Phone Engine Behind a $6.3B Anime Open World
item.description: miHoYo's 2020 action RPG — released September 28, 2020 for Android, iOS, PlayStation 4 and Windows, then PlayStation 5 on April 28, 2021 and Xbox Series X/S on November 20, 2024 — lists Unity as its engine in its infobox, and it still does after reaching $6.3 billion in total revenue by its fourth anniversary in 2024. Genshin Impact Wikipedia Most explainers stop at "anime + BOTW + gacha = money.

item.title: GoHighLevel n8n and Zapier Integration: How to Connect GHL, With Real Workflows (2026)
item.description: Quick answer: Connect GoHighLevel to n8n with the HighLevel node (contacts, opportunities, tasks, calendar) using an OAuth2 Marketplace app, trigger n8n from GoHighLevel with a workflow Webhook action, and use the HTTP Request node for other endpoints. On Zapier, GoHighLevel is the official LeadConnector app.

item.title: Front End Observability: Why Your window.onerror Reports Say "Script error." (and How to Fix Them)
item.description: A practical guide to browser error monitoring with window.onerror, covering the cross-origin blind spot, resource failures that never bubble, and error reports that die when the tab closes. MDN also notes that it only fires for script errors thrown synchronously, such as during initial load or inside event handlers. Assigning window.onerror replaces whatever was there.

item.title: The Hard Part of AI Music Isn't Generation—It's Everything Around It
item.description: It is building a music workflow that behaves like the rest of your production system. What does it cost to keep this feature available through both busy and idle periods, including failed attempts, retries, storage, and engineering time? Treat generation as a job, not an HTTP response Audio generation is long-running work.

item.description: Memory and Knowledge Systems Hybrid Large Language Model (LLM) systems represent an architectural approach that combines the generative and reasoning capabilities of language models with external knowledge, retrieval mechanisms, persistent memory, and executable tools.

I believe VOs will change the way we think about and work with data in Java. I could go on and on about the exciting stuff in recent and upcoming Java releases.

item.title: Beyond code generation: A developer’s guide to agentic engineering
item.description: Agents can help you work more efficiently across all of these stages: Plan, Build, Verify, and Observe. You can use Copilot to pull that scattered context into one place, work through the tradeoffs, and turn the decisions into an implementation plan. Build: Move more than one task forward at a time You’re ready to turn that plan into code.

item.title: What’s fixed in IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3
item.description: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 ships over 1,000 bug fixes and over 300 performance fixes . Among others, Spring Boot inlay hints , property highlighting , and JPA entity analysis no longer stall the editor. We removed excessive index updates when a second project closes during indexing and made the workspace model copy files lazily .

item.title: WebStorm 2026.3: New Design-Code-Production Workflow, JetBrains Air in WebStorm, and More
item.description: Figma Connect, now with the Inspect panel, puts design details right in the chat. Storybook Connect shows you and your agents which components to reuse. The highlights of this release include: JetBrains Air in WebStorm is bringing agentic development directly into your IDE, with your choice of coding agents, support for parallel workflows, and IDE-native review and verification.

item.title: Designing Azure silicon on Azure silicon: EDA workloads on Cobalt 200
item.description: In our silicon design environment, the evaluated EDA workloads ran with 1.30x to 4.15x more performance than on Cobalt 100 across a range of testing scenarios, from simulation to verification to static timing analysis.

item.title: WoW: Forever's massive pre-launch balance patch breaks from the chains Classic power, increasing 'the health of higher level creatures to compensate'
item.description: "Over the course of Beta, we came to the realization that trying to hold ourselves roughly to Classic power budgets for each class meant that every new element we added needed to come at the expense of something else. "Once we have sufficient data from players leveling past 30 and engaging in a wide range of content, we expect that we will do a large tuning pass based on our data.

item.title: Solving Flaky Playwright Tests: How We Automated E2E Generation with an AI Agent and MCP
item.description: Maintaining E2E test suites is one of those engineering tasks we know is critical, but teams often push aside because scaffolding and debugging selectors feels like an endless chore. In this post, I want to break down an architectural approach to solving this: using an autonomous AI agent that explores web apps, infers user journeys, and generates standard Playwright code with MCP support.

item.title: Predicting and detecting failures: How Azure strengthens reliability for mission-critical workloads
item.description: Takeaway : Azure Failure Prediction and Detection (AFPD) is Microsoft Azure’s end-to-end system aiming to catch hardware failures before they interrupt a workload, not after. SAP workloads offer a compelling example of AFPD’s value, illustrating why preventing interruptions matters for mission-critical services.

item.title: The eMudhra Certificate Authority Compromise: What It Means for TeamCity
item.description: Starting with versions 2026.2.2 and 2026.1.6 , TeamCity shows a health report if the installation still trusts affected certificates, along with remediation steps. JetBrains patches TeamCity Cloud, but certificates uploaded to the service still require review. Update your TeamCity agents and review trusted certificates Update Java on every build agent.

item.title: DataGrip and Database Tools User Experience Survey #3 Results
item.description: We’re back with the results of our third DataGrip and Database Tools User Experience Survey. The first part of the survey focused on who you are, which tools you use, and what your daily database work looks like. This year, 84.7% of respondents were satisfied or very satisfied with DataGrip and the built-in database tools.

item.title: Final Fantasy 14: Evercold's story will have a faster tempo, with worldbuilding in side quests, says Yoshi-P—but I'm not sure that was the problem with Dawntrail
item.description: "This time we are putting in serious consideration on the sense of tempo, back at Dawntrail we were being really careful in depicting new lands, new cultures, new encounters and this greatly slowed down the pacing on story progression. However, I don't think the issue in Dawntrail was its over-emphasis on worldbuilding, it was a lack of interest in how that worldbuilding connected to character.

item.title: Empowering AI Agents with agent-desktop
item.description: The agent-desktop repository addresses the challenge of enabling AI agents to effectively interact with desktop applications across different operating systems. By leveraging the OS accessibility tree, it allows agents to read and operate applications without pixel matching, which is often unreliable.

item.title: How do AI agents authenticate? (The problem nobody has solved yet)
item.description: There's no reason agent authentication shouldn't. For agents that need a stable identity across runs, generate once and store the private key. When it calls a tool, the server logs exactly which DID called — not "some agent using the shared service token.

item.title: Di-Hydro Shows How AI and Digital Twins Can Improve Hydropower Operations
item.description: The EU-funded Di-Hydro project is testing how AI, digital twins, forecasting and sensor networks can help hydropower operators make better operational decisions. From fragmented operational data to decision support At the center of the project is the Decision Making Platform (DMP) .

item.title: Your coding agent's sandbox is off. Here's how to turn it on without breaking everything.
item.description: After an hour you either turn the sandbox off or add broad rules ("allow all of ~") that quietly undo it. The agent wrote files that a trusted tool outside the sandbox later acted on: hook configs, IDE task files, git metadata. That is the important lesson for anyone configuring a sandbox: the dangerous permission isn't "write anywhere", it's "write to a file something else will execute later".

item.title: The Local Loop Is the Architecture
item.description: An agent is not a service with a prompt bolted on. That boundary will not appear in production. The thing they can share is a protocol at the edge of the privileged resource, and a loop that runs all three processes where a human can still watch a retry happen.

item.title: WAF is useful, but it does not provide complete protection: What Executives and Managers Need to Understand to Protect Websites and APIs
item.description: When a WAF can identify characteristics of HTTP requests that exploit a particular vulnerability, a rule may block those requests and buy time until the underlying software can be fixed.

item.description: Short answer: use a provider-neutral delivery adapter for email OTPs, and choose a Nodemailer alternative only when its delivery contract fits your media signup flow; the application must still hash, expire, and consume the challenge itself.

item.description: “CLion brings SEGGER’s J-Link, Ozone, and SystemView workflows closer to the development environment while giving agents access to real debugger context. CLion’s new agentic capabilities also show how AI can go beyond code generation and help developers investigate problems directly on real hardware.

item.title: Reconstructing Silent Customer-Support Imports with Structured Error API Capture
item.description: Short answer: Use Node.js to capture the exception at the scheduled-import boundary, post its message, stack, environment, and context to /v1/errors/capture , and preserve a stable run identifier. That gives the next engineer evidence to reconstruct the failed import instead of a bare “job stopped” signal.

item.title: Delivering controlled and concentrated context

By uniting Stack Internal’s new Scopes, an out-of-the-box GitHub connector, and other features like a validation API with Stack Internal Community’s strengthened governance and attribution controls, this launch delivers controlled, concentrated…

item.title: Cutting pull request review time with AI: GitLab, Azure Repos, Bitbucket
item.description: Bitbucket Data Center has no native AI reviewer at all, so review time is set by merge checks and whatever bot you wire in through the REST API. A reviewer with no scoping reviews lock files and generated code forever. GitLab: two review features, two add-on paths GitLab runs one of two code review features depending on your add-on and group settings.

item.title: Meta AI director Rohit Patel leaves to take on Microsoft Office and Google Workspace
item.description: Patel designed Ndoc to be more than just another AI tool layered onto an existing workflow. His desire to open-source this project was partly why he left Meta and decided to go it alone. “Companies are basically attaching AI to spreadsheets and it fills your cells for you,” he said.

item.title: Scale reservoir uncertainty analysis with agile reservoir modeling
item.description: Agile reservoir modeling is the ensemble workflow engine. The workflow tightly connects the tools reservoir teams already use with Azure-scale infrastructure and the governed data services provided by Azure Data Manager for Energy.

item.title: AI on Your Terms: How We See AI in YouTrack
item.description: With YouTrack, you choose whether and how to use AI, while we also make it easier to work with the tools you already trust. Coming soon: Ask YouTrack, an agentic AI chat that understands your work. Delegating task management to coding agents is becoming a common practice, and for such teams, YouTrack evolves from automating individual processes to serving as a shared “agentic database” for agent and human-led tasks.

item.title: 10 Common SaaS Development Mistakes and How to Avoid Them
item.description: Here are ten SaaS development mistakes to avoid and practical ways to build a more reliable, scalable, and sustainable product. Example: A startup planning to build a comprehensive project management platform might discover that its target customers primarily struggle with client approvals and document tracking.

item.title: SlothDesk AI: The Anti-Burnout Desktop Operating Suite That Rewards Laziness (Powered by Google Gemma 2)
item.description: I built SlothDesk AI , a 100% local-first, anti-burnout desktop operating suite powered by Google Gemma 2 open weights . Gemma 2 drafts polite, guilt-free responses that convert 45-minute synchronous meetings into 2-bullet async updates, backed by an explanatory Sloth Principle .
